record.paper_title: Modeling social resilience: Questions, answers, open problems
record.original_question: How can concepts such as robustness and adaptivity be turned into calculable measures for social organizations? The question asks which proxies should be chosen from available agent, relation, and network data and how those choices should be operationalized without reducing resilience to simple topology.

evidence.quote: Questions • How can we turn concepts into measures for robustness and adaptivity?

In order to obtain a measure for resilience, we have to solve two problems: (i) deﬁning diﬀerent proxies to measure robustness and adaptivity based on the available information about agents and their relations, (ii) determining a functional form for resilience dependent on the two dimensions.
Turning concepts into measures is the hardest part of modeling. There are always diﬀerent options to operationalize measures, dependent on available information.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a social organization modeled as a time-evolving multilayer network G_t = (V, E_t, A_t, R_t), where V is a set of agents, each agent i ∈ V carries an attribute vector a_i(t) ∈ A_t (capturing internal states, resources, or roles), and each ordered pair (i,j) carries a relational attribute r_{ij}(t) ∈ R_t (capturing the type, strength, and sign of the relation). Suppose the organization is subject to a class S of exogenous and endogenous shocks s: G_t → G_{t+1} that may delete, add, or perturb agents, relations, and attributes.

Define the resilience of the organization as a scalar functional 
   Res(G_t) = F( Rob(G_t), Adp(G_t) ) ∈ [0,1],
where Rob(G_t) measures robustness (the ability to retain essential structure and function under shocks from S without changing) and Adp(G_t) measures adaptivity (the ability to reorganize agents, relations, and attributes so as to recover or improve function after a shock).

The problem is to:
(a) Construct explicit proxy functionals Rob and Adp from the agent data {a_i(t)}, relational data {r_{ij}(t)}, and network data G_t that go strictly beyond purely topological summaries (e.g., they must use agent- and relation-level information, not only degree distribution, connectivity, or spectral properties of the adjacency matrix).
(b) Specify how each proxy is operationalized as a measurable quantity given partial or noisy observation of agents and relations.
(c) Determine a functional form F: [0,1] × [0,1] → [0,1] combining robustness and adaptivity into a resilience measure, with axiomatic justification (e.g., monotonicity, behavior at the boundary, response to a one-parameter family of shocks).

Provide such proxies and combining functional F, together with conditions under which Res is well-defined, computable from observable data, and not reducible to a function of the network topology alone.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open modeling problem about operationalizing robustness, adaptivity, and resilience for social organizations. No general accepted resolution exists; the literature offers many domain-specific proxies (e.g., redundancy, modularity, response diversity, recovery time) but no canonical, non-topological resilience measure combining robustness and adaptivity for social systems. The problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Modeling social resilience: Questions, answers, open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses turning concepts into measures for robustness and adaptivity and lists this as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The construction of calculable, non-topological resilience proxies is framed as unresolved.
